## Mains side

> **MAINS VOLTAGE. This design has NOT been safety-certified, tested or inspected by anyone.** The mains side (inlet, fuse, relay module, supply terminals, protective earth) must be wired, or checked before first power, by a person competent to do so under your local rules. The electrical verifier checks ratings and that the wires exist; it does not check creepage, enclosure, strain relief, touch protection, or any standard.

- Supply voltage declared: (115.0, 230.0) V. Mains current {'115': 4.94, '230': 2.47} A; inlet rated 10.0 A; fuse T8A (time-lag); cold-start inrush 60.0 A (the fuse riding through it was assumed, I2t not checked).
- **Set the supply's 115 / 230 V selector switch to your mains before first power** (the catalogue's note for the supply: 'set the 115/230 V selector; ring or fork terminals on mains, earth and DC wires'). 230 V on the 115 V setting destroys the supply.
- The inlet's fuse drawer and fuse-link are ordered separately from the inlet (see BOM.md).
- Live terminals that are open to touch in this open-frame design: the inlet's rear quick-connect tabs, the relay module's screw terminals and solder side, the supply's terminal block. Printed hoods in the design cover them: `mains_cover_relay`, `mains_cover_relay_screw_0`, `mains_cover_relay_screw_0_washer`, `mains_cover_relay_screw_0_nwasher`, `mains_cover_relay_screw_0_nut`, `mains_cover_relay_screw_1`, `mains_cover_relay_screw_1_washer`, `mains_cover_relay_screw_1_nwasher`, `mains_cover_relay_screw_1_nut`, `mains_cover_psu`, `mains_cover_psu_screw_0`, `mains_cover_psu_screw_0_washer`, `mains_cover_psu_screw_0_nwasher`, `mains_cover_psu_screw_0_nut`, `mains_cover_psu_screw_1`, `mains_cover_psu_screw_1_washer`, `mains_cover_psu_screw_1_nwasher`, `mains_cover_psu_screw_1_nut`, `mains_cover_inlet`, `mains_cover_inlet_screw_0`, `mains_cover_inlet_screw_0_washer`, `mains_cover_inlet_screw_0_nwasher`, `mains_cover_inlet_screw_0_nut`, `mains_cover_inlet_screw_1`, `mains_cover_inlet_screw_1_washer`, `mains_cover_inlet_screw_1_nwasher`, `mains_cover_inlet_screw_1_nut`. They are open where the wires enter: use fully insulated receptacles on the inlet's tabs and keep the hoods fitted whenever the machine is powered.

### Relay and neutral

The relay module switches the LIVE only and powers its own coil electronics from the mains, so the NEUTRAL is looped through its `N` terminal: one wire inlet N to relay N, a second relay N to supply N, both in one twin ferrule in the relay's N terminal. Without the neutral at the relay it never pulls in. The control board's `PS-ON` pin holds the relay in while the firmware runs and drops it on any shutdown: that relay is the only cut-off for a hotend heater whose MOSFET has failed short (report warning `cutoff_depends_on_mcu`: it does not act if the controller itself has hung).

### Protective earth

- Earth wires in the model: earth to supply (inlet PE to the supply's FG terminal) and earth to frame (inlet PE to the frame stud).
- Frame stud: `earth_stud`, an M5 screw into a T-nut in the outer slot of `frame_bot_left`, ring terminal and star washer under its head; scratch through the anodising under the washer (crimp M5 ring terminals; scratch through the anodising under the serrated washer).
- **The model bonds ONE extrusion.** Every other frame member, the electronics tray, the inlet panel, the motors' bodies, the gantry and the bed carrier are earthed only through anodised extrusion joints, T-nuts, linear bearings or lead-screw nuts, none of which is a reliable bond. Before first power measure continuity from the inlet's earth pin to: each extrusion, the tray, the inlet panel, the supply's case, each motor body, the X beam, the bed plate. Anything above about 0.1 ohm needs its own earth wire. The bed heater is 24 V, but a mains fault to the frame must still blow the fuse.

## Declared but not drawn as wires

- `bed_probe`: a series diode (BAT85 class, cathode to the sensor) is declared in the signal lead; where it is mounted (at the board connector, in the loom) is not modelled.
- `Y motor left`: mirror-image motor on its own driver ([stepper_y1]): invert its dir_pin (or swap one coil pair) so both turn the belts the same way

## Firmware configuration

`printer.cfg` in this folder is a copy of `out/printer_v8_2/electrical/printer.cfg`, generated from the electrical model and loaded by real Klipper in batch mode (klippy ran: True, ok: True, commit 29d4ec2d; that covers: klippy loads every section and plans moves on it; homing and probing against real switches are not exercised).

It holds only what the model knows. Add your host's sections (`[virtual_sdcard]`, `[pause_resume]`, `[display_status]`, macros) yourself. Firmware coordinates: X [0.0, 180.0], Y [34.5, 214.5] is the print area (set the slicer's bed origin and size to match: Y does not start at 0 because the axis has extra travel for the probe).

```ini
max_extrude_only_velocity: 60

# pressure advance: equal to the twin's 32 ms melt-flow lag (direct drive, 0.4 mm nozzle: factory pressure-advance values (fitted_parameters.json: extruder_lag_s), range 0.02 to 0.058 s); not measured on this machine, no sweep run: print a pressure-advance test
pressure_advance: 0.0315
pressure_advance_smooth_time: 0.04

[tmc2209 extruder]
uart_pin: PF2
run_current: 0.400
sense_resistor: 0.110

[heater_bed]
heater_pin: PA1
sensor_type: Generic 3950
sensor_pin: PF3
control: pid
pid_Kp: 69.157
pid_Ki: 4.753
pid_Kd: 251.557
min_temp: 0
max_temp: 90

[verify_heater extruder]
max_error: 120
check_gain_time: 20
hysteresis: 5
heating_gain: 2

[verify_heater heater_bed]
max_error: 120
check_gain_time: 60
hysteresis: 5
heating_gain: 2

[fan]
pin: PA8

# fan 'hotend_fan' is wired to the board's +5 V rail: it runs whenever the machine is powered (no firmware section)

# mains relay ahead of the 24 V supply: energised while the firmware runs, dropped on any shutdown
[output_pin ps_on]
pin: PE11
value: 1
shutdown_value: 0

# input shaper: predicted by the twin, not measured: resonance X 78.0 Hz, Y 72.4 Hz (belt stiffness only, no FEA frame stiffness); damping assumed. Run SHAPER_CALIBRATE
[input_shaper]
shaper_type_x: ei
shaper_freq_x: 98.6
damping_ratio_x: 0.065
shaper_type_y: mzv
shaper_freq_y: 72.8
damping_ratio_y: 0.069

# probe: offsets from the CAD; z_offset from the probe's nominal switching distance on steel (5.0 mm) - set it on the machine with PROBE_CALIBRATE
# that distance: OMRON E2E data sheet CSM_E2E_DS_E_12_4: 5 mm +/-10 % on the standard iron target
[probe]
pin: ^!PG10
x_offset: 0
y_offset: 34.5
z_offset: 3.000
speed: 5
lift_speed: 10
samples: 3
samples_result: median
sample_retract_dist: 2
samples_tolerance: 0.04
samples_tolerance_retries: 3

# Z homes with the probe over the middle of the bed
[safe_z_home]
home_xy_position: 90, 90
speed: 100
z_hop: 5
z_hop_speed: 5

# mesh bounds are probe positions: the bed inset by the probe's edge margin, cut to where the probe can reach
[bed_mesh]
speed: 100
horizontal_move_z: 5
mesh_min: 12, 46.5
mesh_max: 168, 202.5
probe_count: 5, 5
algorithm: lagrange
mesh_pps: 2, 2
fade_start: 1
fade_end: 10
fade_target: 0
split_delta_z: 0.01
zero_reference_position: 90, 124.5
```
